projects.sc: Design advisory and management; SMEs for the steering committee
projects.d: Sumou Boulevard is positioned as the region’s first regenerative city-making development, anchored by a 2 km walkable boulevard — the first flagship project of Paragon-Adeer, a joint venture between Saudi Arabia’s Sumou Investment and Egypt’s Paragon Developments.

projects.n: Cairo Media City Vision Concept Master Plan
projects.sc: Master planning advisory, stakeholder management, archaeology & Egyptology advisory
projects.d: Cairo Media City is positioned at the convergence of Egypt’s emerging high-speed rail network, the site is not peripheral—it is central to the future geography of movement. Within minutes of the Pyramids and directly connected to Greater Cairo and national corridors, this location establishes itself as a new gateway—linking heritage destinations, urban centers, and global access points. This is where arrival becomes identity.

projects.n: Kidana Al Khaif Design Advisory & Review
projects.d: A global panel of experts led by PUD guided the design advisory and review for Kidana Al Khaif across Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafat, bringing expertise in planning, heritage, sustainability and crowd management.
A global panel of experts guided the Jorhum Concept Master Plan, a 990,000 m² mixed-use destination aligned with the Comprehensive Makkah Plan.

Muzdalifah Park is envisioned as a tranquil sanctuary at the heart of the Hajj, offering sacred space for rest, reflection and spiritual connection. The design draws on the ritual of collecting pebbles: from rock to pebbles, from ritual to structure.

projects.sc: Vision master plan and urban development
projects.d: PUD led the development of a future-ready Vision Master Plan for Massoumbou–Diwom, shaping a sustainable, resilient, and high-capacity urban model for Cameroon. The plan integrates land use, mobility, ecology, and infrastructure into a cohesive strategy addressing rapid growth, housing needs, and long-term national development goals.

Majar Al Kabsh is part of the expanded development framework of Mina, enhancing pilgrim flow, spatial experience and operational readiness across the sacred valley. PUD provided the subject-matter experts for the steering committee.

projects.sc: Master planning advisory, local consultant, stakeholder management
projects.d: The Pyramids Plateau Destination Master Plan sets a bold vision to transform one of the world’s most iconic heritage landscapes into a global model for sustainable tourism and inclusive urban development. Spanning from Sphinx International Airport to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Memphis and its Necropolis, the plan safeguards cultural value while unlocking new opportunities for visitors, communities, and Egypt’s future.

projects.sc: Strategic planning and landscape design · 250,000 m²
projects.d: Located at the spiritual heart of Mina, Jabal Thabeer Park is envisioned as a transformative pilgrimage sanctuary— designed to welcome over 50,000 pilgrims daily during the Hajj season, while offering long-term civic value year-round. The project reclaims the mountain as a sacred public space, reinterpreting its symbolic power into a contemporary, inclusive, and terrain-sensitive design.

projects.sc: Master plan, urban and regional planning
projects.d: PUD collaborated with WATG on the master planning of Port Ghalib — reimagining it as a love-inspired destination on Egypt’s Red Sea coast. The project draws from the poetic tale of Ghalib & Budor, embedding the narrative of their journey across the landscape as a foundation for spatial storytelling. Each resort district narrates a chapter of their love story, transforming the terrain into a sensorial journey — from the vibrant Lagoon Village, through the Lowlands Oasis and Plateau Gatherings, up to the regal Highlands Palace, and finally the serene Coral Bay.

projects.n: Sub-Regional Plan for Yanbu, Umluj, Al Wajh & Duba
projects.sc: Local consultant and master planning advisory · ~50,000 km²
projects.d: PUD was commissioned by the Yanbu–Umluj–Al Wajh–Duba Development Authority (YUWDDA), via Metropoli and Typsa, to provide advisory services for regional and local master planning. Strategic sub-regional and local plans for four governorates: Yanbu, Umluj, Al Wajh, and Duba—collectively referred to as the Red Sea Diamond

projects.c: ACUD – Administrative Capital for Urban Development
projects.d: The New Capital is envisioned as a transformative urban initiative — redefining national identity through an integrated, future-ready urban model hosting government, diplomatic, financial and cultural institutions. PUD convened a collective of global strategists to guide master planning for Phases 2, 3 and 4.

projects.n: Al Mashaaer Al Mugaddassah Concept Master Plan
projects.d: A visionary transformation of the Holy Sites of Makkah — Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafat — into a year-round, resilient destination, blending heritage preservation with sustainable innovation for more than 50,000 pilgrims daily.

A multidisciplinary steering group of global experts guided the competition to ensure excellence in urban resilience, cultural authenticity, and long-term operational feasibility It serves as a human-centered transition spine connecting pilgrims with ritual stations through intelligent planning, spatial clarity, and culturally grounded architecture.

The Riyadh Plan Stakeholder Engagement Plan defines the principles, approach, and implementation framework for aligning over 100 governmental and institutional entities in shaping the long-term vision for the capital city. The project ensures active collaboration across ministries, authorities, and private sectors to guide the development of the Riyadh Plan—a comprehensive framework for sustainable growth, economic diversification, and livability enhancement. The plan introduces structured engagement channels, leadership participation forums, and cross-sector communication systems to foster trust, cooperation, and consensus throughout the planning and execution phases.

PUD developed the masterplan for this private estate in Diriyah, Riyadh, integrating natural topography with functional zoning to shape a fully immersive living and leisure environment. PUD’s role focused on orchestrating spatial harmony between private living, agricultural activity, and heritage context—ensuring seamless flow, contextual sensitivity, and long-term adaptability.

PUD led the project as Client Representative and Design Manager, coordinating with WATG, Frantz Slater, and NAGA to deliver a seamless experience across architecture, interiors, and landscape. Zoned into event, family, private, and service areas, the estate is designed for comfort, privacy, and fluid living—guided by climate analysis, contextual integration, and timeless materials.

The Fawaz Alhokair – Palace Extension in Riyadh is a bespoke private residence expansion that redefines intimate luxury through detailed space planning and sensorial materiality. PUD led the Palace Extension for Mr. Abdulmuhsin Al Hokair as Client Representative and Design Manager, overseeing the full design process in collaboration with NAGA Signature Interior Design.

Located on Jumeirah Bay Island, Dubai, this exclusive Bvlgari mansion reflects refined beachfront living—where Italian materiality meets curated space design. The project combines expressive warmth with structured elegance across both architecture and interiors. PUD led the project as Client Representative and Design Manager, overseeing the full design process in collaboration with NAGA Signature Interior Design.

The NEOM Hospital Landscape Conceptual Masterplan establishes a pioneering vision for healing through nature — merging advanced healthcare architecture with restorative outdoor spaces. Designed as a biophilic environment, the landscape becomes an integral part of the hospital’s wellness ecosystem, blurring the line between indoor care and outdoor recovery. Strategically located in Tabuk, the project aligns with NEOM’s regenerative agenda by employing sustainable materials, efficient water management systems, and adaptive vegetation designed for arid climates.

projects.sc: Local consultant, fieldwork surveys, architectural guidelines
projects.d: The guidelines emphasize a balance between tradition and modernity, ensuring that new developments remain sensitive to Najran’s topography, desert landscapes, and agrarian valleys. The design approach celebrates vernacular forms, natural materials, and symbolic heritage patterns while enabling their reinterpretation into scalable, contemporary solutions. The Najran Region Architectural Identity Design Guidelines were developed to strengthen the architectural identity of one of Saudi Arabia’s most historically rich and culturally significant regions.

projects.l: Ras El Hekma, North Coast, Egypt
projects.sc: Advisory lead and masterplan strategist · ~140 ha
projects.d: Azha Ras El Hekma reimagines luxury living through a human-centered masterplan that harmonizes sea, sand, and soul. Rooted in wellness, movement, and environmental sensitivity, the development introduces a new coastal model—where crystal lagoons, walkable green corridors, and inside-out architecture converge to deliver year-round vitality. Through curated zones, immersive journeys, and smart connectivity, PUD transforms a raw terrain into a living seafront tapestry of experience, balance, and belonging.

projects.c: Ministry of Housing, Utilities & Urban Communities
projects.d: Alamein Riviera blends luxury tourism, ecological intelligence, and cultural depth into a year-round Mediterranean icon—revitalizing the edge of New Alamein through immersive placemaking, smart mobility, and landmark hospitality.

The Al Khafji (Project Line) Concept Master Plan is a forward-thinking coastal development located in the Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia, near the border with Kuwait. Commissioned by the Public Investment Fund (PIF) and managed by the Gulf Coast Development Company (GCDC), the project envisions transforming Al Khafji into a sustainable, mixed-use coastal destination that harmonizes economic vitality, tourism, and environmental stewardship. Developed in association with WATG, the master plan reimagines Al Khafji’s coastal edge as a connected urban corridor — balancing tourism, residential, and economic nodes within a linear city framework inspired by Saudi Arabia’s new generation of transformative developments.

Gargoub New Port City is a strategic vision masterplan located on Egypt’s northwestern Mediterranean coast. With a waterfront extending 23 km and a total area of 170 km², the city is planned as a new economic and commercial hub, integrating tourism, industry, education, and residential life. The masterplan introduces diverse districts, including a commercial port, touristic marina, financial and residential zones, educational institutions, agro-industrial clusters, wellness and health services, and leisure resorts.

projects.sc: Master planning, landscape and environmental design · 7 km²
projects.d: Heliopark is a 7 km² smart and green residential community in New Cairo, designed to accommodate 10,000 residential units alongside a mix of regional services, community facilities, and commercial hubs. Commissioned by Hassan Allam Properties, one of Egypt’s leading real estate developers, the project was envisioned as a flagship development integrating sustainability, environmental planning, and modern urban living. The masterplan emphasizes livability, resilience, and sustainability, creating a balanced urban fabric that incorporates green buildings, energy efficiency measures, and climate-conscious planning.

projects.sc: Strategic planning, master planning, sustainability SME
projects.d: The Sharaan Nature Reserve is one of four landmark master planning projects led by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU). Known globally for its extraordinary natural heritage and cultural landscapes, the reserve required a visionary master plan that balances ecological preservation with sustainable tourism development. WATG, Prior + Partners, and an expert consortium of international and Saudi specialists in planning, ecology, and engineering collaborated to create a master plan that integrates world-class conservation strategies with innovative eco-tourism experiences.

The Khaybar Heritage Area Master Plan is part of the Royal Commission for AlUla’s broader vision to transform AlUla into a globally recognized cultural and heritage tourism destination. The project reinvigorates the Khaybar Heritage Area by connecting its volcanic landscapes, archaeological sites, and unique natural assets into a unified visitor journey. Phased development begins with immersive visitor experiences such as aerial tours of volcanic craters and archaeological wonders, extending AlUla’s day-trip offerings.

projects.sc: Infrastructure master planning and city planning
projects.d: In line with Saudi Arabia’s establishment of the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) in 2017, the AlUla County Infrastructure Master Plan was developed to safeguard and shape the future of AlUla as a globally significant cultural and tourism destination. Covering approximately 25,000 km² and serving a population of about 45,000 across 51 settlements, the project integrates archaeology, tourism, culture, education, arts, and lifestyle into a cohesive framework for sustainable development. The master plan’s focus is on infrastructure modernization and strategic city planning, ensuring that AlUla’s transformation into a global hub for heritage and leisure is aligned with sustainability principles and Vision 2030 goals.

projects.sc: Policy and planning advisory, framework planning
projects.d: AlUla County Framework Plan & Guidelines is a strategic planning initiative established by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) to safeguard the region’s heritage and guide its sustainable development. Covering an area of approximately 25,000 km², the plan provides a comprehensive framework for county-wide zoning, infrastructure development, and cultural preservation. AECOM was engaged to provide programme management consultancy services, supporting RCU’s Development Asset Management Department while also advising on city planning and infrastructure.

projects.sc: Strategic land-use planning and asset optimisation
projects.d: The Saudi Railway Organization (SRO) identified the need to assess and optimize the strategic and economic value of its extensive land and property assets across the Kingdom. This Strategic Plan was initiated as part of Saudi Arabia’s National Transformation Program (NTP) to unlock the potential of SRO’s assets for development, investment, and economic growth. The plan aimed to evaluate high-value land parcels, recommend optimal development opportunities, and establish a market-driven, best-use strategy.

Taj Al Riyadh is envisioned as a pioneering residential-lifestyle destination nestled in the northeast of Riyadh, aligning with the aspirations of Vision 2030 to elevate urban living quality and diversify housing typologies. Commissioned by Al Mozaini Real Estate and supported by the Ministry of Housing, PUD was entrusted with crafting a holistic, human-centered master plan that merges natural terrain, socio-cultural relevance, and modern urban aesthetics. Rooted in the desert topography and climate, the design weaves urban fabric with green resilience, offering shaded promenades, interconnected neighborhoods, and a vibrant commercial spine.

projects.c: Al Mozaini for Real Estate Development
projects.d: Al Jawhara Residence contributed to Jeddah’s transformation into a modern yet culturally anchored urban center. The development set a precedent for high-quality, mid-density residential living that aligns with Saudi Vision 2030 goals — enhancing livability, sustainability, and community well-being.

projects.n: Jazan City for Primary & Downstream Industries
projects.d: Jazan City for Primary & Downstream Industries (JCPDI) is part of Saudi Arabia’s strategic program to drive inward investment, regional economic growth, and employment creation. Positioned as the Kingdom’s leading industrial city for energy-related industries, JCPDI is designed to provide an unparalleled environment for downstream industrial development, sustainable growth, and global competitiveness. The Royal Commission for Jubail & Yanbu (RCJY), building on its successes in Jubail and Yanbu, was entrusted by Royal Decree to manage, operate, and deliver the vision for JCPDI.

Fanarah is envisioned as a distinctive, year-round coastal tourism destination, seamlessly integrating diverse residential, hospitality, and leisure experiences within an exceptional natural setting along Egypt’s northwestern Mediterranean coast. Anchored in sustainable tourism principles, the master plan balances economic vitality, environmental stewardship, and community life. Its design philosophy celebrates the site’s rare turquoise bays, unspoiled beaches, and layered coastal topography, delivering a harmonious blend of nature, culture, and luxury

projects.sc: Feasibility study, design and tender documents
projects.d: The Suez Canal Tunnels project consists of the design, feasibility study, and tender preparation for three tunnels under the Suez Canal, providing a vital link between the Sinai Peninsula and mainland Egypt. Strategically located at Port Said, the tunnels enhance territorial connectivity, improve transport efficiency, and contribute to Egypt’s long-term economic and population redistribution strategy. The multidisciplinary study incorporated road and railway integration, geotechnical analysis, and environmental assessments to ensure sustainable and feasible outcomes.

projects.sc: Project management and strategic urban advisory
projects.d: Commissioned to address an urgent planning gap, the Jeddah Spatial Framework Plan (SFP) was developed within a tight 6-month window to guide critical infrastructure projects across the city—specifically the Middle Ring Road (MRR), stormwater network, and redevelopment of unplanned “Ad Hoc” areas. The plan was crafted to align these interventions within a broader metropolitan spatial logic, ensuring coherence with Jeddah’s long-term urban vision

This project explored development opportunities for prime coastal land adjacent to the private residence of HRH Prince Talal Bin Abdulaziz in Hurghada. PUD, in collaboration with AECOM, conducted detailed site analysis, economic assessments, and development feasibility studies to identify the most viable and sustainable options. The study proposed four alternative scenarios balancing hospitality, residential, and mixed-use opportunities, while preserving the natural Red Sea setting and respecting the site’s strategic location.
A boutique hotel on Egypt’s Red Sea, designed by PUD.
A residential and commercial tower in Zamalek, Cairo, designed by PUD.

projects.n: Regional Vision for Tourism, North-West Coast
projects.c: Tourism Development Authority, Ministry of Tourism
projects.sc: Regional vision and strategic master planning
projects.d: PUD was commissioned to prepare the regional vision and general master plan for the northwest coast of Egypt, a region rich in natural beauty and cultural heritage. This large-scale development plan focused on eco-tourism and environmental tourism, leveraging the area’s diverse landscapes — from desert plains and wildlife habitats to pristine sandy beaches and rare vegetation. The vision aimed to deliver a sustainable tourism model that empowers local communities, celebrates heritage, and triggers a catalytic development chain reaction, positioning Ras El Hekma as a vibrant tourism hub while supporting population decentralization from Cairo To balance large-scale tourism development with environmental preservation and cultural identity, creating a destination rooted in place while open to global visitors.

The Green Star Hotels Initiative was launched to promote sustainable tourism in Egypt by introducing environmentally sound practices within the hospitality sector. With Egypt’s tourism industry being a vital economic driver but also an environmental risk factor, the project aimed to improve the ecological performance of hotels, reduce water and energy waste, and align the sector with international sustainability standards. More than 200 hotels nationwide earned the Green Star certification after meeting rigorous audit and training requirements.
Headquarters and research centre for the Hurghada Environmental Protection and Conservation Association, an NGO working in marine and land conservation across the Red Sea Governorate.

projects.sc: Master planning, urban design and landscape
projects.d: Al Ain El-Sukhna Tourist Resort occupies a prime strip along the Red Sea coast, designed to maximize both land use efficiency and environmental comfort. Villas are located in areas with generous breadth, while duplexes occupy narrower zones. The southern section of the resort is dedicated to open-air recreational and sports facilities.

The Tehran Laleh Hotel is a landmark mixed-use complex that integrates hospitality, residential, office, commercial, and recreational functions at the heart of downtown Tehran. Positioned at the intersection of two major streets and overlooking the city’s central Laleh Park, the development is designed as an urban extension of the park, seamlessly blending landscape with architectural form. Conceived with futuristic and unconventional design elements, the project aims to symbolize modern Iran while offering a multi-functional hub for residents, visitors, and business professionals.

projects.c: Al Aqeelah for Real Estate Development
projects.sc: Master planning, urban design and architecture · 500,000 m²
projects.d: Maria Heights is a 500,000 m² luxury resort located atop Al-Sayeh Mountain in Nassra, designed to provide a premium tourism and residential experience. The development includes a presidential resort, a variety of villas and small apartment buildings, as well as commercial and entertainment facilities

Alex Gate is the winning proposal in a national competition for the master planning of a 500-feddan mixed-use development in West Alexandria. The site is strategically located adjacent to Carrefour, facing the international park and airport, and overlooking Lake Maruit. The project is designed as the first visual marker of urban development for travelers arriving from Cairo via the Alexandria desert or agricultural road.

projects.sc: Master planning, urban and architectural design · 86,000 m²
projects.d: Set on a prime coastal site overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, the Investors Tourism Village covers 86,000 m² and establishes a contemporary leisure and hospitality hub in New Damietta City. The development includes 74 semi-attached villas, each designed to maximize sea views, alongside 50 hostels and an array of commercial and leisure facilities. With its coastal orientation, the village integrates residential, tourism, and recreational functions to create a vibrant mixed-use destination.

projects.c: Al Aqeelah for Real Estate Development
projects.sc: Master planning, urban design and urban planning
projects.d: New Najaf City is envisioned as a major urban expansion to the existing city of Najaf, serving as the new cultural, economic, and business center for the region. Strategically located around Najaf Lake, the city offers direct views of the sacred shrine of Imam Ali and integrates its spiritual significance into the overall design. The master plan maximizes the use of existing natural and cultural assets, with the lake and surrounding areas designated for recreational and tourism functions.

projects.n: City of Knowledge, University of Islamic Sciences
projects.c: Al Aqeelah for Real Estate Development
projects.d: The City of Knowledge is envisioned as a state-of-the-art educational hub reflecting Iraq’s cultural and religious heritage. The University of Islamic Sciences sits at its core, designed to represent both Iraq’s Islamic and Arabian identity while offering a modern academic environment. Spanning an area of 3.5 x 2.5 km, the master plan integrates educational facilities, residential districts, commercial zones, and recreational spaces.

projects.sc: Master planning, architecture and hospitality design
projects.d: Located in the heart of Hurghada’s tourism center, the Pyramisa Apartment Hotel and Shopping Mall is a mixed-use hospitality destination designed to combine leisure, accommodation, and community living. The project integrates a luxury apartment hotel, villas, employee housing, and retail facilities within a cohesive, resort-style environment.

projects.n: Strategic Plans for Egypt’s Rural Settlements
projects.sc: Principal in charge, urban planning · 10 villages
projects.d: The project involved the strategic planning of 10 rural villages across Sharkiya, Qualyoubia, Gharbiya, Dumyat, and Beheira governorates, including Akyad Al-Bahariya, Awlad Seif, Balashone, Kotamat Al-Ghaba, Abo Hamar, Senbo El-Kobra, Shaheedy, Kafr El-Wekala, Kofoor El-Ghab, and Kom Esho. PUD developed directive plans to regulate urbanization, protect agricultural land, and improve the quality of life in rural Egypt.

projects.sc: Urban design, architecture and master planning
projects.d: The Royal Oasis Residential, Shopping, and Hotel Complex was inspired by traditional Egyptian architecture, reinterpreted through modern typologies, sustainable materials, and environmental solutions. The project integrates residential, hospitality, leisure, and retail functions into a vibrant and self-sufficient community. Landscape features, water elements, and green zones were strategically introduced to create a healthier microclimate, while delivering a harmonious and comfortable living environment.

projects.c: Hegaz Company for Real Estate Investments
projects.sc: Urban and architectural design · 3 km of coast
projects.d: The Sukhna Heights Tourist Resort is located along a 3 km stretch of the Gulf of Suez in Ain El-Sokhna. The development is uniquely built on mountainous terrain, creating a distinctive urban form that blends sea views with elevated residential and hospitality zones. Designed as part of the wider Suez Gulf tourism strategy, Sukhna Heights integrates luxury resorts, leisure facilities, and mixed-use spaces to attract year-round tourism.

projects.c: Saudi Egyptian Company for Investment & Development
projects.sc: Master planning and urban design · 230 ha
projects.d: Samator Tourist Center is a 230-hectare coastal resort destination strategically located along the Gulf of Suez at Ain El-Sokhna. Designed to accommodate over 16,000 visitors, the master plan integrates two hotels, a motel, holiday residences, sporting clubs, water parks, and regional commercial centers. The resort’s distinctive design leverages the site’s natural topography, creating a unique urban form complemented by vibrant, green landscapes

projects.c: Al Madinah Central Area Development Authority
projects.d: PUD designed a series of hotels, residential, and commercial buildings in Al Madina Al Munawara, blending contemporary Islamic architecture with the city’s spiritual and cultural environment. The designs respect the contextual conditions of the holy city, reinforcing its role as a hub for pilgrims and residents while delivering modern comfort and functionality. [ Concept Designs for Al Hashimi Hotel, Al Kattan Hotel, Al Zahem Hotel, Shirbini Hotel, Basharia Hotel, Detailed Designs for Al Hashimi, Al Kattan, Al Shirbini, Al Zahem Hotels — Commercial and Residential Complexes ]

projects.c: Samala & Alam El Roum for Urban Development
projects.sc: Competition master plan and architecture (first prize)
projects.d: Building on the success of Marina Al-Alamein, Marina Matrouh aimed to extend Egypt’s tourism development along the Mediterranean coast, creating a unified architectural identity rooted in the region’s character. Spanning 1,000 feddans with 8 km of beachfront, the plan introduced a vibrant mix of activities to attract a wider tourist base, reduce seasonality, and foster year-round economic vitality. The project vision blended hospitality, sports, culture, and leisure into a cohesive masterplan that reflects both environmental sensitivity and cultural harmony.

projects.sc: Regional planning and urban design · 30 ha
projects.d: Marina Latakia is a 30-hectare Mediterranean coastal resort located 10 km north of Latakia city. Designed as a high-capacity tourism hub, the development integrates luxury hospitality, serviced apartments, employee housing, and a variety of holiday home types. Recreational, cultural, and commercial facilities are strategically placed to create a vibrant and accessible destination for both visitors and residents

The Hilton Dahab Village Hotel lies along the Gulf of Aqaba in Sinai, east of Egypt. Completed in 1997, the project has been acclaimed for its harmonious integration of natural and built environments — where the sea, mountains, and desert converge in a unique topography. The masterplan defines a self-contained resort village that celebrates the fluid relationship between land and water.

projects.c: NUCA, Ministry of Housing and New Communities
projects.d: Spanning multiple phases over nearly two decades, Marina El-Alamein stands as Egypt’s first large-scale tourism development and a landmark example of sustainable coastal planning. Conceived to make the Mediterranean’s pristine beaches accessible to Egyptian citizens while attracting international tourism, the project integrates social, economic, and environmental objectives in one cohesive masterplan. Today, the center hosts over 7,000 holiday homes, multiple hotels, and attracts more than 35,000 tourists annually, supporting 10,000 jobs in the tourism sector

projects.sc: Initial concept and master plan, landscape
projects.d: The Marakia Tourist Village was the first large-scale tourism project on Egypt’s North West Coast (NWC), commissioned by the government to stimulate private sector development and set a benchmark for coastal tourism policy. Located between the 50th–52nd km west of Alexandria, the project aimed to ease tourist pressure on Alexandria, accommodate day-trippers from Cairo and the Delta, and promote the NWC as a strategic leisure hub. PUD Consultants developed the initial design concept in alignment with national tourism policy, integrating natural resources (beach, sand dunes, agricultural land) into a holistic plan.

Located along Lake Nasser in Aswan, Tut Amoun Village was Egypt’s first tourist village, designed to harmonise with Nubian character and cultural values. It was awarded Best Tourist Project in Egypt and recognised internationally at the Rome Biennale 1992.

projects.c: Ministry of Housing and New Communities
projects.d: PUD’s early landmark project for the North West Coast region marked a decisive step in Egypt’s tourism and urban development strategy, aiming to channel growth away from the densely populated Nile Valley into new coastal communities. Covering 65 km east-to-west and 7 km north-to-south, the plan integrated housing, employment, and tourism within a unified urban framework. The development vision balanced tourist attractions, services, and facilities with agricultural and industrial components, fostering sustainable communities.

news.h: SHARE Architects brings its first African forum to Cairo, at the Grand Egyptian Museum
news.x: Dr. Amr Attia joins the local organising committee for the 13–14 December forum.
b: For the first time, the SHARE Architects forum comes to Africa — and it lands in Cairo, at the Grand Egyptian Museum, within sight of the Pyramids. Over two days, architects, planners and developers from across the region and beyond will meet to discuss how the next generation of cities and buildings should be shaped.

Dr. Amr Attia, CEO of PUD Consultants, sits on the local organising committee alongside Prof. Iman Gawad, Karim El Hayawan and Dr. Tamer Elgabaly. For PUD, the forum is a chance to bring the international design conversation to Egypt, and to put Egyptian practice at the centre of it.

The programme is built around four themes that reflect where the region is heading: public architecture and the design of facades; housing and mixed-use development; capital, design and nation-building; and sustainability and artificial intelligence in design.

The theme of capital and nation-building speaks directly to PUD’s own work — from strategic advisory on the New Administrative Capital to destination planning at the Pyramids. Sixty years after PUD was founded in Cairo, hosting this conversation at home feels like the right way to mark the anniversary.

news.h: “Making a New Capital City Work”: Dr. Amr Attia speaks at SHARE Georgia 2026
news.x: Among 30 speakers from 10 countries in Tbilisi.
f: Making a New Capital City Work
b: At SHARE Georgia 2026 in Tbilisi, Dr. Amr Attia joined 30 speakers from 10 countries to talk about one of the hardest questions in city-making: how do you make a new capital city actually work?
Drawing on PUD’s strategic advisory for Egypt’s New Administrative Capital, the talk looked beyond the master plan, at what it takes for a new capital to grow into a living, working city.

The forum brought together some of the most influential names in global architecture, with keynotes from Herzog & de Meuron, Foster + Partners and Henning Larsen. Among the reflections shared after the forum, Alexander Novikov singled out Dr. Attia’s presentation as one of its highlights.
For PUD, conversations like this are part of how the firm works: sharing what we learn on the ground, and bringing back ideas from peers around the world to the projects we shape at home.

news.h: Pyramids Destination: a scenario tool shaped with WATG and PUD’s local expert team
news.x: Field work and archival photography reshaped the role of Dahshur.
f: Local expert team, led by Dr. Amr Attia
b: Planning a destination around the world’s most visited ancient site means making choices that will shape it for generations. To make those choices clearer, the team behind the Pyramids Destination framework built a scenario decision tool: a way to test how different strategies for access, visitor flows and development would play out across the wider landscape.

The work was developed with WATG, alongside a local expert team led by Dr. Amr Attia of PUD. Local knowledge proved decisive. A field route through the landscape, together with archival photographs shared by Dr. Fekri Hassan, changed the team’s understanding of Dahshur — and with it, the role Dahshur plays in the framework.
It is a reminder of something PUD has believed since 1966: good plans are not drawn from a distance. They come from walking the land, reading its history and listening to the people who know it best.

news.h: AKHET: the Tourism Master Plan of Pyramids Destination
news.x: Completed with WATG for the Ministry of Housing and the Ministry of Tourism.
f: Ministry of Housing · Ministry of Tourism
b: AKHET is the tourism master plan for Pyramids Destination — a long-term vision for how visitors will experience the Giza plateau and the landscape around it. The name comes from the ancient Egyptian word for the horizon, the place where the sun rises and sets.

Completed in December 2024 for the Ministry of Housing and the Ministry of Tourism, the plan was developed with WATG, with PUD as part of the core team. It sets out how to protect the last surviving wonder of the ancient world while creating a world-class destination around it: new arrival experiences, carefully placed hospitality, and a landscape restored with respect for its history.

For PUD, AKHET brings together six decades of work in heritage, tourism and regional planning — and a commitment to making places that honour the past while serving the people who visit and live there today.

news.h: Sumou Boulevard launches: EGP 7 billion booked in 24 hours
b: Sumou Boulevard, by Paragon-Adeer, set out to be the region’s first regenerative city. Its launch showed how much appetite there is for that idea: EGP 7 billion in bookings within 24 hours, and demand 6.1 times greater than the units on offer, with 3,343 unit requests.

Perhaps the most telling number is who is buying. Seventy percent of buyers are under 40 — a young generation choosing a place designed around nature, community and long-term value rather than short-term returns.
PUD provides the subject-matter experts for the project’s steering committee, helping to keep the regenerative vision at the heart of every decision as the city moves from plan to reality.

news.h: A wonderful close to an amazing project: the Pyramids master plan is delivered
news.x: A world-class team with WATG and Wimberly Interiors.
b: In December 2025, Dr. Amr Attia marked the close of the Pyramids master plan with a simple message: it had been an honour to work with a world-class team.

The project brought together WATG and Wimberly Interiors with PUD, Luxury Partners and Shaker Consultancy Group, guided by local knowledge keepers and cultural interpreters including Dr. Fekri Hassan, Dr. Michael Jones and Dalila ElKerdany. Team members described the aim as restoring one of the world’s most significant cultural landscapes with reverence and sensitivity, so that it can anchor a new era of tourism.
For PUD, it is the kind of project that defines a practice: global expertise and local understanding working as one, in service of a place that belongs to everyone.

news.h: PUD celebrates 60 years of shaping sustainable cities
news.x: From a founder’s vision in 1966 to 150+ projects across 11 countries.
b: In 1966, Prof. Abdallah Abdel Aziz Attia founded PUD on a simple belief: that planning should begin with people and with the natural and cultural environments they live in.

Sixty years later, that vision continues through Prof. Dr. Amr A. Attia. PUD has delivered 150+ projects across 11 countries and 60+ cities — from Alex to Aswan, across the Red Sea to Saudi Arabia, and beyond.
The anniversary is a moment to look back, and to ask the question that has always driven the firm: what should we build next?
